a01.title: Broken Access Control
a01.description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data or performing a business function outside the user's limits.

a02.title: Cryptographic Failures
a02.description: Cryptographic failures arise when sensitive data is not properly protected. This includes failures to encrypt sensitive data, use of weak or broken cryptography, and improper key management.

a03.title: Injection
a03.description: Injection flaws occur when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. The attacker's hostile data can trick the interpreter into executing unintended commands or accessing data without proper authorization.

a04.title: Insecure Design
a04.description: Insecure design is a broad category representing different weaknesses, expressed as 'missing or ineffective control design.' Insecure design is not the source for all other Top 10 risk categories.

a05.title: Security Misconfiguration
a05.description: Security misconfiguration can happen at any level of an application stack, including network services, platform, web server, application server, database, frameworks, custom code, and pre-installed virtual machines, containers, or storage.

a06.title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
a06.description: Components, such as libraries, frameworks, and other software modules, run with the same privileges as the application. If a vulnerable component is exploited, it can make the application easier to attack and lead to data loss or server takeover.

a07.title: Identification and Authentication Failures
a07.description: Identification and authentication failures were previously known as Broken Authentication. These failures allow attackers to compromise passwords, keys, session tokens, or exploit other implementation gaps to assume users' identities.

a08.title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
a08.description: Software and data integrity failures relate to code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations. This includes insecure deserialization, unverified updates, and lack of code signing.

a09.title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
a09.description: Security logging and monitoring failures were previously known as Insufficient Logging & Monitoring. These failures allow attackers to further attack systems to cause additional damage or cover their tracks.

a10.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
a10.description: SSRF flaws occur whenever a web application is fetching a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL. It allows an attacker to coerce the application to send a crafted request to an unexpected destination.

sqlInjection.title: SQL Injection Lab
sqlInjection.subtitle: Interactive environment for learning SQL vulnerabilities
sqlInjection.protectionText: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) or ORM libraries (Prisma, Sequelize, TypeORM). Never insert user input directly into SQL queries via string concatenation.
